doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: Listening to the concerto recording
summary: Rowe plays an excerpt of Levy's concerto and praises its tunes and the harmonica's unison tone colors.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I became stuck with it. I had to keep playing it. And one of my own parameters about writing music is a goal of when it’s over people will have part of it in their head. And that certainly applied here. The other thing that struck me was every time you played the harmonica in unison with various instruments it’s like a new tone color was invented.
And that’s like a real advantage, right? Like you’ve got this sort of built-in new sound every once in a while because as far as I know no one else is doing this exact thing.
